model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; earnings to common after capital retained for balance-sheet growth at the CET1 target, net debt zero; equivalent to residual income on tangible book)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (the CSV Revenue basis: FY2025 5,853 + 2,394 = 8,247). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported; FY0 = H1-26 actual 4,451 (Q1 2,168, Q2 2,283; SEC XBRL InterestIncomeExpenseNet + NoninterestIncome) + Q3E ~2,330 (guided NII +2.5-3.5% QoQ, fees flat on record Q2) + Q4E ~2,370. Using FY2026E puts year 1 = FY2027, one year after the fiscal year that is now 75% reported.
inputs.share_count_basis: 421.18m common shares outstanding at 24 Jul 2026 (10-Q Q2-2026 cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~3m dilutive RSU/PSU awards (Q2-26 diluted weighted 427m vs period-end 422.7m, net of in-quarter buybacks). Held FLAT: SBC is charged in the flows, and buybacks ($1,050m FY24, $600m FY25, $525m H1-26) are how the FCFE is returned, not a separate source of value.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt held at ZERO by construction. Deposits ($185.6bn at 30 Jun 2026) and borrowings (long-term debt $15,190m + short-term $1,159m) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and due from banks ($1,219m) is held against that funding. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to common equity at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~= net income to common ~2,180 (H1-26 1,038 annualised with Q3/Q4 NII growth) less capital retained ~640 (= NI x g/ROTCE at 4% balance-sheet growth, 13.7% ROTCE) to hold CET1 in the 10.0-10.5% target band (10.4% at Jun-26). Cross-check: FY2025 NI to common 1,688 less dividends 755 and buybacks 600 = 333 retained; H1-26 NI to common 1,038 less dividends 396 and buybacks 525 = 117 retained while CET1 slipped to 10.4% on loan growth -- i.e. recent distributions run slightly ahead of organic FCFE.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory OCF (FY2025 2,211, FY2024 2,001, FY2020 111) is dominated by loans-held-for-sale and trading movements and is not free cash flow for a bank; reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense: FY2025 $120m, FY2024 $97m, FY2023 $87m; H1-26 $82m (FY2026E ~$140m, 1.5% of revenue). Net-share-settlement withholding (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation) was $6-26m a year to 2024 and is not tagged after mid-2024; immaterial and not added.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income is the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026E ~$1.0bn ($300m Q1, $225m Q2 per Q2 release, similar pace H2). Treated as distribution of FCFE, not modelled separately.
inputs.preferred_note: Preferred stock $2,111m par at 30 Jun 2026; preferred dividends $138m FY2025, $33m/quarter 2026 (PreferredStockDividendsIncomeStatementImpact). Charged in the flows via the cash_tax_rate_path (see tax note), so value is to COMMON equity and no preferred deduction is made in the bridge.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:03Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime)
inputs.book_value_anchor: 30 Jun 2026: total stockholders' equity 26,183 less preferred 2,111 = common equity 24,072; less goodwill 8,220 and other intangibles 105 = tangible common equity 15,747 (before DTL on intangibles) = $37.25 per period-end share (422.7m). AOCI is -2,261 (unrealised securities/swap losses) and sits inside TCE; CFG is a Category IV bank that excludes AOCI from CET1, so it does not constrain distributions today and its pull-to-par is an unmodelled upside to book (not to FCFE). Price 65.53 = 1.76x TBV. Q2-26 ROTCE 13.9% (company), 12.2% Q1-26; FY2025 ~11%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year Treasury ~4.2% (Sept 2026) + beta ~1.15 (regional bank, rate- and credit-cycle levered; 2023 regional-bank run showed the tail) x 5.0% US ERP = ~10.0%. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle and NIM risk is charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches) are inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin; immaterial relative to $24bn common equity. No lease line, no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income equals income attributable to CFG.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity through the component engine, as NAB.AX (2026-09-24) and IAG.AX (2026-09-23). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NI x g/ROTCE is the clean-surplus equivalent and runs through the validated slider engine. First valuation of CFG (no memory entry, no prior DCF). Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income; ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS SBC, as % of revenue (FY2025: 2,328 + 120 = 2,448 / 8,247 = 29.7%; H1-26: 1,405 + 82 = 1,487 / 4,451 = 33.4%; Q2-26 34.4%; FY2026E ~34.3%); sbc_pct_path 1.5%; da_pct = 0 (D&A and intangible amortisation are real bank costs inside noninterest expense); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to grow tangible common equity with the balance sheet (g_bs x TCE / revenue), holding CET1 at target; cash_tax_rate_path = income tax (~23%, Q2-26 22.3%, FY2025 21.3%) PLUS preferred dividends ($132m) as a share of pre-tax income, so the flow is earnings to COMMON; wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0. Implied ROTCE paths (NI to common / average TCE, TCE starting ~16.0bn at Dec-26): base 14.9% FY27 -> 15.5-15.8%; bull 16.0% -> 18.6%; bear 10.9% -> 12.4%. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (15.6 - 3.0)/(10.0 - 3.0) = 1.80x x $37.25 = ~$67 base; market 1.76x TBV prices roughly the base case. Price is the regular close, not volatile. Filings not text-extracted; all figures from SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 759944) through the Q2-2026 10-Q filed 2026-08-03.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 11.9% diverges >30% from equity 5yr 3.0%: FY2020 EPS ($2.22) is a COVID reserve-build trough, so the 5yr EPS rate flatters. 3yr rates (FY2022 -> FY2025: revenue +0.9%, EPS -1.8%) capture the 2023-24 deposit-cost squeeze. Equity growth is held down by buybacks ($4.4bn FY2021-H1-26) and AOCI swings, not weak earnings.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (OCF is loan/trading flow); fcf fields left null. FY2022 revenue step-up is the HSBC branch and Investors Bancorp acquisitions (shares 427m -> 495m). FY2026 is tracking ~+11% revenue on NIM recovery (guided 3.22-3.27%).

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +7%: NIM guided 3.30-3.50% vs 3.22-3.27% FY26 (~+3-4% NII from margin, mid-point discounted) plus ~4% earning-asset growth and fee growth from Private Bank/wealth/capital markets offset by CRE runoff. Tapers to 3% terminal (US nominal GDP ~4% less a mature bank's share loss).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin + SBC. FY26E 34.3%; Reimagine the Bank ($450m pretax by 2028, ~4pp of revenue gross) largely reinvested; provisions normalise from ~0.40% of loans toward ~0.45% through-cycle. Steady 34.5% pre-tax margin = ~15.5% ROTCE, below management's 16-18% FY27 target: CFG has historically lagged its return targets.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained = balance-sheet growth (4%, 4%, 4%, 3.5% x3, 3% x4) x tangible common equity, as % of revenue; implied payout 74% FY27 rising to ~82%.
base.cash_tax_rate_rationale: ~23% income tax + preferred dividends ($132m) as a share of pre-tax income (3.9% FY27 falling as pre-tax grows).
base.narrative: NIM guidance is met near the low end, Private Bank and fees grow high-single-digit, credit normalises gently, and ROTCE settles ~15.5%.

bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: Top of NIM guide (3.50% FY27), Reimagine benefits drop through, provisions stay ~0.35-0.40% of loans; ROTCE 16% FY27 rising to ~18.6% -- management's 16-18% target delivered and sustained.
bull.capex_rationale: Faster balance-sheet growth (5%, 5%, 4.5%, 4.5%, 4%, 4%, 3.5%, 3.5%, 3%, 3%) retains more capital.
bull.narrative: The Private Bank scales to 15-16 offices at ~25% ROE, record capital-markets and wealth fees persist, NIM reaches 3.5%, and AI productivity lifts ROTCE into the 16-18% target band and holds it -- closing the return gap to higher-quality regional peers.

bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY27-28 US slowdown: provisions rise to ~0.8-0.9% of loans (C&I and office CRE), faster Fed cuts compress asset-sensitive NIM toward 3.1%, fees (capital markets, mortgage) cyclical. Recovers only to ~29.5% pre-tax, ROTCE ~12.4% -- the pre-2026 CFG.
bear.capex_rationale: Balance-sheet growth 2%, 1.5% in the downturn, then 3%/2.5%.
bear.narrative: The Fed cuts faster than the NIM guide assumes and a credit cycle arrives in 2027: office CRE and C&I charge-offs rise, capital-markets fees fall, CET1 at the low end of its band halts buybacks, and CFG reverts to its long-run 11-12% ROTCE.

scenario_narratives.base: Citizens delivers most of its NIM recovery (3.22-3.27% FY26 to ~3.35% FY27) as swap and securities repricing roll through and deposit betas hold in the high-40s. Private Bank, wealth and capital-markets fees grow high-single-digit while CRE runs off. Reimagine the Bank savings are largely reinvested; credit costs drift up modestly to through-cycle. ROTCE settles around 15.5% -- a real improvement on FY2025's ~11% but short of the 16-18% target, consistent with the company's record of trailing its return goals. At ~1.8x tangible book that is roughly what the market already pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management hits the top of its FY27 NIM range (3.50%), the Private Bank reaches 15-16 offices at ~25% ROE and drives outsized low-cost deposit growth, AI productivity ($450m by 2028) drops largely to the bottom line, and credit stays benign (NCOs in the 30s bp, strong DFAST results supporting buybacks). ROTCE reaches ~18.6% and holds, re-rating CFG toward higher-return peers.
scenario_narratives.bear: A faster Fed easing cycle compresses the asset-sensitive margin just as a 2027 slowdown lifts C&I and office CRE losses; capital-markets and mortgage fees fall; CET1 at 10.4% (low end of target) forces a buyback pause. Revenue stalls for two years, provisions roughly double, and ROTCE reverts to ~12% -- the pre-2026 run rate -- so tangible book compounds slowly and the multiple compresses toward ~1.3x TBV.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: a ~15x levered balance sheet with residual office CRE, an asset-sensitive NIM tied to the Fed path, and CET1 at the low end of its band make a credit/rate cycle a genuine tail (the 2023 regional-bank run is recent). Bull cut to 25% because it needs management to hit a ROTCE target it has historically missed AND credit to stay benign. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank's free cash flow to shareholders is the earnings it can distribute after retaining enough capital to grow its balance sheet at its CET1 target. Value = PV at a 10% cost of equity of earnings to common (after preferred dividends) less that retention; deposits and borrowings are operating funding and are never deducted. The value driver is sustainable ROTCE versus cost of equity: at ~15.5% base ROTCE and 3% growth, fair value is ~1.8x tangible book.
key_risks_to_valuation: ROTCE path: each 1pp of sustained ROTCE is worth ~$5/share (~0.14x TBV)
Fed path and deposit betas driving the FY27 NIM guide (3.30-3.50%)
Credit cycle: office CRE and C&I charge-offs (NCOs 37bp Q2-26)
CET1 at 10.4% vs 10.0-10.5% target limits buyback flexibility
Basel III endgame AOCI inclusion for Category IV banks would pull the -$2.3bn AOCI into CET1 and constrain distributions
Cost of equity: 10.0% single rate; +/-1pp moves value roughly 15-20%
